criteria.title: Professional positioning
criteria.purpose: Can the reader identify the kind of work and understand the intended professional direction?
criteria.positive: A description connected to actual roles and relevant work lets the reader identify the professional contribution. More than one specialty is compatible with clear positioning.
criteria.problem: Descriptions that conflict with the inspected experience, or obscure the work relevant to the stated purpose, support a bounded clarification. A preference for a narrower identity does not.

examples.adequate: Product Designer supported by interaction design and systems work.
examples.problematic: An unsupported executive title contradicts the recorded role.
examples.uncertain: The target is not supplied, so specialization for a specific vacancy remains conditional.

route.heading: Chapter 7: Interviews, scorecards and design evidence

criteria.title: Relevant experience
criteria.purpose: Can relevant experience be located and connected to the stated purpose?
criteria.positive: Relevant responsibilities or examples are identifiable. General assessment can establish what is demonstrated without inventing a target or interpreting omitted work as inability.
criteria.problem: Important supplied evidence is difficult to locate, or the document claims a requirement is met when the inspected evidence contradicts it. Unrelated experience is not inherently harmful.

examples.adequate: A systems role points to component decisions and governance.
examples.problematic: An asserted essential qualification conflicts with the supplied record.
examples.uncertain: A relevant capability is not described and must be clarified rather than declared absent.

criteria.title: Chronology and factual consistency
criteria.purpose: Are dates, employers, roles and project chronology understandable and internally compatible?
criteria.positive: The inspected chronology is understandable and has no demonstrated consequential contradiction. Overlapping consulting and employment can be compatible.
criteria.problem: An actual contradictory date, employer or sequence warrants correction. A gap, overlap or older role alone does not establish a defect.

examples.adequate: Employment and a concurrent independent project are labeled distinctly.
examples.problematic: The same role has incompatible start dates in supplied passages.
examples.uncertain: A project date is not supplied, so its relationship to a later launch is unresolved.

criteria.title: Individual contribution
criteria.purpose: Can individual responsibility be distinguished from the work of a team?
criteria.positive: The text identifies personal decisions, responsibilities or outputs in their team context. Collaboration does not require claiming sole ownership.
criteria.problem: A consequential ownership claim contradicts the inspected material, or unclear contribution prevents evaluating relevant responsibility. Missing ownership evidence is a clarification.

examples.adequate: Owned interaction design while engineers deployed the service.
examples.problematic: Claims sole implementation while the supplied case assigns implementation elsewhere.
examples.uncertain: A team launch is described without identifying the candidate contribution.

criteria.title: Supported claims and outcomes
criteria.purpose: Do consequential claims stay within the scope of their supporting evidence?
criteria.positive: Claims are compatible with the available evidence and distinguish prototypes from production, observed results from forecasts, and contribution from unsupported causality.
criteria.problem: A demonstrated contradiction is material. Missing measurement or deployment evidence supports a clarification, not an accusation of dishonesty.

examples.adequate: Evaluated a prototype with a stated test scope.
examples.problematic: Calls the same five-user prototype an established production deployment without reconciling phases.
examples.uncertain: A causal business outcome is asserted but the evidence establishes only participation.

criteria.title: Scope and seniority
criteria.purpose: Does the record make the scale, responsibility and level of work understandable?
criteria.positive: Concrete scope and decisions support an understanding of responsibility. Preserve official titles and explain functional scope where useful.
criteria.problem: An inflated or conflicting rank warrants correction. Different employer title systems or a broad title do not independently establish a problem.

examples.adequate: A senior role explains independent ownership and collaboration scope.
examples.problematic: A staff title is attributed to an employer that supplied a different official title.
examples.uncertain: A senior title appears without enough scope to assess the target expectation.

criteria.title: Supporting evidence and proof navigation
criteria.purpose: Can the reader locate an appropriate supporting example when the task calls for one?
criteria.positive: Relevant evidence is inspectable in the supplied material or clearly routed to an appropriate example. Confidential work can use a bounded account without disclosure.
criteria.problem: A broken inspected route, irrelevant linked case or unclear evidence path supports a bounded improvement. Do not claim a link works without inspecting it.

examples.adequate: A role points to a supplied case describing decisions and contribution.
examples.problematic: An inspected portfolio link resolves to an unrelated project.
examples.uncertain: A URL is present but its destination has not been inspected.

criteria.title: Text extraction and reading order
criteria.purpose: Does an inspected original file produce the important text in an understandable order?
criteria.positive: An observation derived from the supplied original establishes relevant content and reading order. A local extraction is evidence about that file, not every ATS.
criteria.problem: Demonstrated missing or scrambled important text supports a correction. Silence or a quick rejection does not establish a parsing failure.

examples.adequate: The supplied PDF extraction preserves names, roles and bullets in order.
examples.problematic: An inspected extraction omits the contact details visible in the original.
examples.uncertain: Only pasted text is supplied, so original-file extraction cannot be checked.

criteria.title: Sections and employment information
criteria.purpose: Are the important sections, employers, titles and dates identifiable?
criteria.positive: A reader can associate employment information with its role and inspect relevant sections. Conventional headings can help without imposing a universal template.
criteria.problem: Ambiguous association or demonstrated missing necessary information supports a bounded change. An unconventional but understandable arrangement is not a defect. Type size, density and layout are presentation choices that support at most an optional note unless the inspected original loses or misassociates text.

examples.adequate: Each role has an identifiable employer and dates.
examples.problematic: A date cannot be associated with either of two roles.
examples.uncertain: An excerpt excludes the employment section, so completeness is unestablished.

criteria.title: Truthful terminology
criteria.purpose: Does terminology describe actual experience in language relevant to the intended work?
criteria.positive: Terms are supported by responsibilities and examples. Useful naming can connect genuine experience to a target without repetition or invented credentials.
criteria.problem: Unsupported credentials or misleading skill labels justify correction. Different wording alone does not prove an employer search missed the candidate.

examples.adequate: Design systems is connected to component and governance work.
examples.problematic: Adds an unheld certification to match a posting.
examples.uncertain: No target or actual search query is supplied, so discovery effects remain uncertain.

criteria.title: Headline and About
criteria.purpose: Do supplied identity sections communicate the work and connect it to evidence?
criteria.positive: Headline and About have understandable professional purpose and align with Experience. Concise or varied wording can be effective.
criteria.problem: Consequential contradiction or obscured meaning supports a bounded change. A slogan preference or absence of a recommended section is not automatically harmful.

examples.adequate: A headline names product design and About explains systems experience.
examples.problematic: Headline asserts a current role contradicted by the supplied chronology.
examples.uncertain: Only Experience was supplied, so headline and About cannot be assessed.

route.heading: Chapter 13: Profile sections and professional evidence

criteria.title: Experience and role context
criteria.purpose: Do Experience entries identify responsibilities and distinguish official title from explanatory scope?
criteria.positive: Roles connect claims to contribution and context. Relevant functional clarification preserves the underlying facts.
criteria.problem: Incorrect roles, incompatible dates or obscured relevant responsibility support correction or clarification.

examples.adequate: An official title is retained with a truthful explanation of product ownership.
examples.problematic: An imported résumé created an employer role that the person never held.
examples.uncertain: The Experience entries are absent from the supplied excerpt.

route.heading: Chapter 13: Profile sections and professional evidence

criteria.title: Skills supported by experience
criteria.purpose: Do inspected skill labels have credible support in experience or examples?
criteria.positive: Explicit skills are compatible with actual work. Labels are descriptions rather than proof of mastery or a controllable ranking formula.
criteria.problem: A demonstrably unsupported credential warrants correction. A missing endorsement or inferred skill is not evidence of poor competence.

examples.adequate: A systems skill is supported by component design work.
examples.problematic: Lists a qualification contradicted by the supplied facts.
examples.uncertain: Skill labels are not included in the supplied capture.

route.heading: Chapter 13: Profile sections and professional evidence

criteria.title: Featured and proof navigation
criteria.purpose: Where work samples are relevant, can supplied profile routes lead to appropriate evidence?
criteria.positive: Selected evidence has a clear purpose and inspected routes work. Featured is optional and evidence can be available through other appropriate sections.
criteria.problem: An inspected broken route or confusing case selection can justify improvement. Absence of Featured alone does not justify a defect.

examples.adequate: Experience links to a supplied case even without Featured.
examples.problematic: An inspected Featured item opens a deleted page.
examples.uncertain: A supplied text capture omits Featured and link destinations.

route.heading: Chapter 13: Profile sections and professional evidence

criteria.title: Discovery terminology
criteria.purpose: Do truthful labels make relevant professional experience understandable and searchable?
criteria.positive: Names, roles and skills describe genuine work using understandable terminology. Keep profile discovery separate from recruiter evaluation.
criteria.problem: Misleading identity fields or unsupported labels justify correction. Views, silence or a small analytics change do not establish a causal profile remedy.

examples.adequate: The profile uses a supported design-systems label.
examples.problematic: Adds misleading terms to the name field.
examples.uncertain: A recruiter search configuration is unavailable and no rank can be inferred.

route.heading: Chapter 12: Recruiter search, filters and discovery

criteria.title: Required and preferred criteria
criteria.purpose: Are target requirements distinguished from preferences and assessed against their actual wording?
criteria.positive: The supplied target identifies relevant requirements and the comparison respects their conditions. Employer clarification is needed where wording is ambiguous.
criteria.problem: Treating a preference as mandatory or declaring eligibility without evidence supports correction or clarification.

examples.adequate: Deployment ownership is preferred and interaction design is required.
examples.problematic: Declares the applicant ineligible solely for a preferred tool.
examples.uncertain: No vacancy text or sufficiently defined target is supplied.

criteria.title: Direct and transferable evidence
criteria.purpose: What direct, transferable, missing or contrary evidence supports the target comparison?
criteria.positive: The comparison identifies actual work and explains any transfer without claiming identical domain experience.
criteria.problem: Unsupported equivalence or a contradiction warrants a finding. An unfamiliar industry is not automatically disqualifying.

examples.adequate: Complex operator software provides transferable workflow experience.
examples.problematic: Claims regulated-domain experience that the inspected history contradicts.
examples.uncertain: Evidence supports adjacent work but the required domain responsibility is unclear.

criteria.title: Target-relevant supporting examples
criteria.purpose: Do supporting examples address the target evidence requirements?
criteria.positive: Examples demonstrate relevant decisions and contribution. Match depth to actual employer expectations rather than one company rubric as a universal standard.
criteria.problem: A supplied case fails to establish a consequential requirement or contradicts its claim. Missing proof remains a clarification.

examples.adequate: A systems case explains governance relevant to the supplied role.
examples.problematic: The selected case establishes prototype work while the claim asserts deployment ownership.
examples.uncertain: The target asks for portfolio evidence but the case was not supplied.

criteria.title: Dates and titles across assets
criteria.purpose: Are consequential dates, employers and titles compatible across supplied versions?
criteria.positive: Differences are compatible or explained by version, official title or audience context. Exact wording need not be identical.
criteria.problem: Inspected incompatible facts justify correction after chronology and version are checked.

examples.adequate: A functional headline differs from the accurate official employment title.
examples.problematic: The same role has conflicting end dates in current supplied assets.
examples.uncertain: Only one asset was supplied, preventing cross-asset comparison.

criteria.title: Ownership and outcomes across assets
criteria.purpose: Do scope, ownership and outcome claims remain compatible across supplied assets?
criteria.positive: Claims describe compatible contribution and outcomes with phase distinctions where needed.
criteria.problem: An actual contradiction supports correction. Stronger language with unestablished causality may instead need clarification.

examples.adequate: The résumé names design responsibility and the case credits engineering deployment.
examples.problematic: One asset states minimal onboarding and another claims none for the same measured scope.
examples.uncertain: Different project phases may explain apparently conflicting deployment statements.

criteria.title: Versions, emphasis and audience
criteria.purpose: Are apparent discrepancies explained by dated versions or compatible emphasis?
criteria.positive: Current and historical records are distinguished. Different emphasis for different audiences is allowed without assuming synchronization.
criteria.problem: A stale current record or material contradiction needs a bounded response. Do not edit historical submissions to erase their evidence.

examples.adequate: An older submission remains preserved while the current profile uses updated wording.
examples.problematic: Calls an old captured profile the verified live state.
examples.uncertain: The capture date or current account record is unavailable.

route.heading: Chapter 10: Configuration, permissions and limits of inference
